text:
Aisha: quick follow-up from today's all-hands — I promised a short live Q&A on engineering process (release cadence, oncall, quality bars, SLAs). Drop one-line questions and we'll answer here.
Jordan: can someone TLDR the new release cadence? missed the demo slide.
Marco (CTO): TLDR — week-based cadence: feature branches -> merge to main on Tues -> canary deploy Wed morning -> full rollout Fri noon PST. Major platform releases still gated quarterly. See RFC: https://internal.redwood/rfcs/release-cadence.
Sam (QE): are there hard quality gates? which tests block a release?
Leah (VP Eng): quality bar = all critical/major tests green + no new SEV1/SEV2 regressions in last 48h + perf smoke within 10% of baseline. Blocking checks are unit+integration+smoke; e2e flakiness must be under threshold or flagged. Codeowner signoff still required for infra changes.
Jordan (Product): quick follow — who gets to approve an exception if e2e is flaky but business needs the release?
Leah (VP Eng): exceptions go to the release approver pool (leads from Eng, SRE, QE, and Product). We log the exception, reason, and rollback plan in the release ticket.
Ravi (SRE): oncall question — will the oncall rota or SLOs change with weekly releases?
Marco (CTO): SLOs unchanged for now. We're shifting runbook ownership so the release owner does the initial post-deploy verification; SRE oncall remains escalation for infra incidents.
Ravi (SRE): for clarity — handover checklist: release owner posts: `release-ticket, canary-metrics, rollback-plan`. Oncall-Bot can auto-ping if canary error rate > 2%.
Oncall-Bot: @Ravi will be paged if canary error rate exceeds 2% for 5m during Friday rollouts.
Sam (QE): any change to how QE should run performance checks?
Leah (VP Eng): QE to run the perf smoke suite against canary traffic window. We added a small perf gate in CI: `perf_smoke_threshold=1.10` (10% allowable). If exceeded, block and require mitigation plan.
Jordan (Product): SLA ops — customers asked for 99.9 for dedicated customers. Is that formal now?
Marco (CTO): yes, Dedicated customers moving to contractual 99.9 for uptime; hosted tiers remain best-effort with published metrics. Support/finance will follow up with legal on language.
Jordan (Product): thanks — when do sales get the official blurb?
Leah (VP Eng): Friday morning we push the doc to the partners folder; I'll loop in Sales.
Aisha: tiny ask — can folks drop any follow-ups here by EOD, we'll synthesize into a short action doc and post in #eng-ops and the all-hands notes.
Marco (CTO): small note — starting next sprint we'll try a one-week canary ramp for big infra changes; aim is to reduce rollbacks.
Sam (QE): noted. I'll add perf suites to the release checklist template.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for `release/2026-11-04` — 10% traffic route.
Ravi (SRE): if deploy-bot reports anomalies, immediate rollback criteria: latency p95 > baseline*1.25 OR error rate > 2%.
Aisha: thanks everyone, I'll compile and post. :memo:
